Required destination_field is "blue_goal"; drawer_position must remain > 0.26 m, with red on or being released over its pad. If blue is still free and source variation dominates, hand off to h01 (particularly source rotation) or consider h04 for its source-to-goal corridor prior, while retaining the no-OOD-evidence caveat. validation.guidance: Validated in distribution at 10/12 final successes (83.3%). Entry requires drawer_position > 0.26 m, red being released/settled on its pad, blue outside or held, and source_object="blue" plus destination_field="blue_goal". Avoid it for large source or destination displacement, global collision-free routing, long open-loop correction, or recovery after drops, re-grasps, or impacts; eight-step local increments can drift. Do not use the auxiliary phase class as a success or contact signal. Watch for phase/geometry disagreement, blue failing to co-move after closure, drift away from source or destination, IK/limit issues, red or drawer regressions, and lip/wall contact. Replan every eight executed actions. Hand off to h02 when blue is stably carried toward the drawer, and to h01 for large free-source displacement; h04 is the corridor-specialized alternative for source-to-goal translation. End only on framework-observed simultaneous task success. No recovery or learned successor is established.

validation.exit_rule: drawer_position >= 0.29 at the final state (the demonstrated open stop is 0.30)
validation.guidance:
**Use:** Drawer-frame Cartesian prior requiring accurate `drawer_origin_world_m`, unit `drawer_orientation_wxyz` (local -X is opening), and `desired_open_position_m > 0.26` (trained at 0.300 m). Its documented purpose is following a reliably calibrated displaced drawer, but no displaced-drawer rollout was validated. In the nominal in-distribution test it passed only 3/12 runs (25%); the three passing final positions were 0.29976–0.30000 m. Therefore it is not the nominal default and no broadly reliable regime beyond those individual runs was established.

**Avoid:** Prefer H03 for nominal geometry. Avoid H01 with uncertain/stale drawer calibration, large or unreachable displacement, missed/blocked front contact, or independently displaced/noisy red pose. Entry after nonzero opening and shifted cabinets are design intentions, not validated conditions.

**Failure recognition:** Require the physical final/current drawer position, not a transient maximum. Six failed runs crossed 0.29 m and then ended at 0.16345–0.26554 m; three other failures never crossed 0.29 m. Treat regression, lack of progress, inconsistent TCP/front geometry, calibration jumps, red/TCP misalignment, closure without red co-motion, a drop, IK nonconvergence, or limit contact as failure and stop/replan rather than repeating nominal commands. A closed gripper is not grasp proof.

**Handoff:** The validated open-skill exit is `drawer_position >= 0.29` at termination. The documented overlap with `red_transfer` covers actions 230:470: an earlier switch is represented once the drawer is above 0.26 m and red is exposed; the stronger nominal switch is after drawer motion is near zero, front contact is released, and closed fingers are accompanied by observable red/TCP upward co-motion. Success of the successor composition was not validated here.

validation.exit_rule: drawer_position >= 0.29 at the final state (the demonstrated open stop is 0.30)
validation.guidance:
**Use:** Fresh-TCP local-increment prior requiring accurate drawer origin/orientation and desired opening (trained at 0.300 m). Its documented niche is a modest arm/path deviation in an otherwise training-like scene, including local correction from fresh measured TCP state. Such perturbed entries were not separately validated. In-distribution it passed 6/12 runs (50%), so treat it as a monitored secondary option rather than the nominal default.

**Avoid:** Do not use it as recovery for large deviations, a missed handle/front, blocked drawer, distant/unreachable objects, or accumulated pose drift. Prefer H01 only when reliable cabinet displacement is the dominant consideration, and H03 for nominal geometry. Local increments are not globally object-displacement invariant.

**Failure recognition:** Every validation run reached at least 0.29 m once (first crossing at steps 201–223; maximum 0.300 m), but six ended below the exit threshold at 0.13102–0.28257 m. Thus a transient opening is not completion. Watch for repeated local motion without drawer progress, subsequent drawer regression, unexpected drawer motion, growing TCP/front or TCP/red error, closure without red co-motion, red drop, IK nonconvergence, or limit contact; replan instead of allowing drift to accumulate.

**Handoff:** For validated completion, verify `drawer_position >= 0.29` at termination. The 230:470 overlap permits transfer to `red_transfer` after opening above 0.26 m and red exposure; the cleaner cue is a stable drawer, released front, closed fingers, and observed red/TCP upward co-motion near the initial lift. The validation did not test the composed handoff.

validation.exit_rule: drawer_position >= 0.29 at the final state (the demonstrated open stop is 0.30)
validation.guidance:
**Use:** Primary nominal-geometry policy. It takes no caller arguments and emits absolute world-frame TCP targets, with relational conditioning and an auxiliary nominal-phase classifier. From each policy-specific training-segment entry, it passed 12/12 in-distribution runs (100%): all first crossed 0.29 m at steps 200–230 and ended at 0.29954–0.30000 m, with zero reported IK-unconverged steps. This is the strongest validated choice for the nominal cabinet calibration and physically coherent demonstrated approach/pull/release/red-approach phases.

**Avoid:** Absolute world targets can fail if the cabinet has moved. Do not infer competence for shifted/rotated cabinets, arbitrary intermediate starts, missed front contact, blocked pulls, misgrasps, drops, collisions, or recovery; none was validated. Although its documents permit entry at a causally recognizable intermediate phase, validation began only at the training-segment entry. The phase class is neither contact proof nor an execution gate.

**Failure recognition:** Stop/replan if drawer progress, finger state, and selected action become incoherent; the drawer fails to reach/retain the required opening; front dragging continues; TCP/red alignment does not improve; closure is not followed by red/TCP co-motion; red drops; or IK fails/reaches limits. Gripper closure and phase prediction alone do not establish success.

**Handoff:** The validated skill exit is `drawer_position >= 0.29` at termination. The fully supervised 230:470 overlap allows an earlier `red_transfer` switch after the drawer exceeds 0.26 m and red is exposed. Prefer the stronger handoff after near-zero drawer motion, front release, and closed fingers with observable red/TCP upward co-motion. No successor rollout was evaluated in this validation.

validation.exit_rule: red on the pad and drawer_position > 0.26 at the final state
validation.guidance: Low-confidence red-centered specialist, not a routine default. In the fixed in-distribution protocol it passed 4/12 runs. Invoke only from its supported state: drawer_position strictly >0.26 m, red exposed, and a reliable current red pose, with entry at the drawer front or during red approach/contact/lift. Its red-frame representation is intended for red-pose displacement, but no displaced-red validation exists. Avoid after red release, when blue/post-release geometry dominates, when the red pose is stale, or when transformed targets may be obstructed/unreachable. Treat lack of red/TCP co-motion after closing, IK non-convergence, low carried-red motion into furniture, red outside the pad or following retreat, or drawer_position falling to <=0.26 as failure. Validation failures ended either with red off-pad (5 runs) or red on-pad but the drawer below threshold (3 runs); several had hundreds of unconverged IK steps. Three failed runs transiently met the exit rule and later lost it, so verify the fixed condition at handoff rather than accepting a transient pass. Handoff: require red contained on the pad and no longer following TCP while drawer_position remains >0.26; the retained overlap can continue into blue pickup, with observed blue/TCP co-motion on initial lift as the cleanest cue to switch to blue_insert.

validation.exit_rule: red on the pad and drawer_position > 0.26 at the final state

The destination-centered representation is intended for pad-relative placement; relocated-pad benefit is not validated. validation.exit_rule: red on the pad and drawer_position > 0.26 at the final state

The representation is designed so pickup-side targets follow the source and insertion-side targets stay goal-anchored, but robustness to translated sources or changed source-goal separation was not tested out of distribution and must not be assumed. Avoid it when source or drawer rotation is the main change, when predicted corridor progress alpha selects an implausible anchor, for unreachable/collision-prone geometry, or as drop/impact recovery. Inspect published alpha/target diagnostics: warning signs include red-release targets being dragged toward blue, pickup targets moving toward the drawer before a secure grasp, lack of blue/TCP co-motion, IK failure/limits, lip/wall approach, drawer_position <= 0.26 m, red leaving its pad, or missed final blue bounds. Treat that as one observed failure pattern, not a general threshold. Refresh source and goal endpoints every eight actions. Hand off to h02 once blue is stably carried near the drawer; use h01 when source rotation dominates and h03 for small fresh-TCP corrections. Completion is only the simultaneous framework success condition; there is no learned successor.

validation.exit_rule: drawer_position >= 0.29 at the final state (the demonstrated open stop is 0.30)
validation.guidance:
**Use:** Phase-adaptive Cartesian prior that uses a calibrated drawer frame early and observed red frame late. It requires all six call arguments; training used desired opening 0.300 m and gate values `red_phase_min_open_m=0.280`, `red_phase_clearance_m=0.280`, and `red_phase_xy_radius_m=0.140`. Its documented purpose is reachable drawer and independent red displacement when both object frames and gate cues are reliable. However, no such displacement was validated, and nominal in-distribution performance was only 2/12 (16.7%; passing finals 0.29503 and 0.29885 m). No reliable general operating regime was established, so reserve it as an explicitly unvalidated alternative rather than a default.

**Avoid:** Prefer H03 at nominal geometry, especially when drawer/red observations or gate cues are uncertain. Avoid noisy calibration, gate-boundary states, large/unreachable shifts, missed/blocked pulls, collisions, misgrasps, drops, and recovery attempts. The active-frame mechanism is constructive design evidence, not rollout evidence of displacement robustness.

**Failure recognition:** Nine of the ten failed runs crossed 0.29 m and later ended below it; failed final positions ranged from approximately 0.00005 to 0.28250 m. Treat transient crossing as insufficient. Also stop for repeated active-frame changes/chatter, target jumps near the gate, return toward or dragging of the drawer front, nonshrinking TCP/red XY error, closure without red/TCP co-motion, drop, IK residual/nonconvergence, or limit contact. IK diagnostics alone do not prove outcome: unconverged steps appeared in both passing and failing runs.

**Handoff:** Verify `drawer_position >= 0.29` at the validated exit. The 230:470 overlap permits `red_transfer` once opening exceeds 0.26 m and red is exposed, but the red-frame gate itself is not readiness proof. The stronger cue is a stable drawer, released front, closed fingers, and observed upward red/TCP co-motion. The composed handoff was not validated here.

validation.exit_rule: red on the pad and drawer_position > 0.26 at the final state

At the represented action-230 entry use drawer_clear; later use only the phase matching observed geometry: red_acquire for red approach/contact/lift, red_place_release for held-red transport through release and initial clear, bridge_to_blue only after release and vertical clearance, and blue_acquire for transit/approach/closure/lift on blue. Wrong-phase discontinuity, absent object/TCP co-motion, premature/failed release, crossing red before clearance, return toward red during transit, blue not under TCP at closure, drawer_position approaching 0.26, or IK non-convergence are failure cues. Both validation failures retained an open drawer (0.2723 and 0.2876 m) but ended with red off-pad; intermittent IK non-convergence also occurred in some passing runs, so pad containment remains decisive. Handoff: red_place_release may continue while red is held/touching in the successor overlap, followed by bridge_to_blue and blue_acquire; the clean nominal switch to blue_insert is after red is contained and stationary, drawer_position >0.26, and blue/TCP co-motion confirms initial lift.

validation.exit_rule: red inside the central buffer region at the final state

validation.exit_rule: blue at its goal region and red still in the buffer at the final state
validation.guidance:
**Validated reliability:** Best treated as a specialized, non-default option. It retained the complete exit in 7/12 in-distribution runs. Blue was at goal in 11/12 and red remained buffered in 8/12; four runs reached the exit predicate transiently but ended with red outside the buffer, while one never reached it and ended with blue off goal. Thus 11/12 had a `first_pass_step`, but only 7/12 passed at the final state.

**When to use:** Call with `target_object=blue`, `destination_goal=blue_goal`, and `context_object=red` when red is low/settled near the central buffer, blue is clearly the intended object, and two causal observations distinguish blue from red. Its blue-object-frame prior is intended for source-side blue displacement around pickup, but no displaced-source validation exists; do not treat that expected invariance as measured reliability. On nominal in-distribution geometry, prefer h03 based on validation.

**Avoid / detect failure:** Avoid ambiguous object identity, a held blue already near destination, drops, collisions, wrong-object grasps, disturbed red, or unreachable/large corrections. Stop on wrong-object approach, any unexpected red movement, blue not following a closed gripper, release outside goal, blue remaining attached after opening, or persistent IK residuals/limit issues. Replan the blue frame from current observations for each execution chunk.

**Handoff:** Switch to `place_red` when blue is visibly stationary inside `blue_goal` and the gripper is open and TCP clear. Because several runs only passed transiently, do not assume that continuing the overlap will preserve the exit. If continuing to the later supervised handoff, require buffered red to visibly follow the closed gripper upward; closure alone is not proof of grasp. Preserve the two-frame causal history across the switch.

validation.exit_rule: blue at its goal region and red still in the buffer at the final state
validation.guidance:
**Validated reliability:** Do not use as the default complete-skill policy. It passed the final exit in only 1/12 in-distribution runs. Blue was nevertheless at goal at the end of all 12 runs, and every run recorded a `first_pass_step`; the 11 final failures were specifically that red was no longer in the buffer. This supports blue-placement behavior in these runs but not reliable retention of the full exit through continued execution.

**When to use:** Call with `target_object=blue`, `destination_goal=blue_goal`, and `context_object=red` only as the specialized goal-frame option when blue is plausibly already held—visibly elevated, co-moving with the gripper, en route, or near its destination. It is designed for late/intermediate entry and destination-relative placement. Shifted-goal performance was not tested, so that benefit is an unvalidated prior rather than a demonstrated result.

**Avoid / detect failure:** Avoid relying on it for source acquisition or displaced-source pickup, and avoid prolonged continuation when preserving buffered red is essential. Stop if blue does not co-move, descent is offset from `blue_goal`, the gripper opens while blue is high, blue remains attached after opening, red is disturbed, or IK residuals/limits persist. Co-motion is a routing cue, not contact truth; this package has no established drop, collision, or wrong-grasp recovery.

**Handoff:** Use the documented core cue as soon as observed: blue stationary inside `blue_goal`, gripper open, and TCP clear; preserve causal history and switch to `place_red`. Given the 12 transient versus 1 final pass pattern, do not assume the supervised tail will preserve the exit. If the tail is intentionally used, switch only after buffered red visibly follows the closed gripper upward, never on closure alone.

validation.exit_rule: blue at its goal region and red still in the buffer at the final state
validation.guidance:
**Validated reliability:** This is the default choice for entry states matching the validated distribution. It passed the complete final exit in 12/12 runs: blue at goal and red still buffered in every final state. First passage occurred at steps 312–395. This evidence is limited to replayed entry states from its own training segments; it does not establish perturbation recovery or out-of-distribution robustness.

**When to use:** Call with `target_object=blue`, `destination_goal=blue_goal`, and `context_object=red` when two causal frames show a physically plausible phase from final red release through blue relocation, or the supervised red-pickup tail, with object identity, gripper width, and relative motion observable. Its fresh-TCP incremental prior is intended for modest intermediate or handoff offsets, but those offsets were not separately tested.

**Avoid / detect failure:** Do not extrapolate this result to gross source displacement, large destination displacement, arbitrary large corrections, drops, collisions, wrong-object grasps, or disturbed red. Stop if local corrections leave demonstrated support, TCP/object geometry matches no represented phase, blue does not follow the gripper, red moves unexpectedly, goal release fails, or IK residuals/limit contacts persist. Compose every executed slot from the freshly measured TCP; do not advance history during denoising or accumulate predicted poses.

**Handoff:** Switch to `place_red` when blue is visibly settled inside `blue_goal` and the gripper is open and TCP clear. If the successor is not ready, the policy may continue only through its supervised terminal overlap; the later valid cue is buffered red visibly moving upward with the closed gripper. A close command alone is not a grasp predicate. Preserve causal history across the switch.

No run had an unconverged IK step, so IK convergence alone did not distinguish success. Do not use as the routine in-distribution choice. Its object-equivariant representation is designed for a reachable displaced or yawed red source, but that benefit was not validated out of distribution; consider it only as a closely monitored, structurally matched fallback when such source variation dominates and stronger validated alternatives are unsuitable. Enter only with blue descending to or settled in blue_goal, red observable/reachable in the central free area, and finite robot/object state. Avoid unstable blue, noisy or unreachable targets, obstacles, ambiguous nearest-object selection, missed attachment, or slip. Recognize failure if the reference selector oscillates, red does not rise after closure, red separates in transport, release misses full goal containment, either block is disturbed on retreat, or the final predicate remains false—especially the validated pattern blue_at_goal=true/red_at_goal=false. Terminal handoff: there is no successor; stop only when both red_at_goal and blue_at_goal are observed. Gripper sign, reference identity, open fingers, or a high retreat is not by itself success evidence.

**Measured scope/reliability:** Passed 12/12 (100%) fixed-protocol runs from its own demonstrated segment entry at action 180, the strongest in-distribution result. Every run ended with all 12 particles in the bowl and the container upright. First satisfaction occurred between rollout steps 967 and 2270 within the 2340-step budget, so the validation does not support assuming uniformly early completion.

**Use when:** Prefer as the default for states matching the validated nominal entry: the source is securely held and lifted/lifting, the source-to-TCP relation is stable, bowl/source/TCP/particle poses are reliable, and targets are reachable with safe clearance. Its absolute bowl-frame source-pose prior directly anchors container orientation. Adaptation to displaced bowls or atypical rigid grasps is a structural expectation only; neither was tested out of distribution.

**Avoid/switch when:** Avoid on uncertain/sliding grasps, rapid source-to-TCP transform change, unreliable poses, unsafe bowl clearance, particles outside the bowl, persistent IK residuals/limits, or independently changed bowl/return geometry. For a highly ambiguous partial-discharge entry where local correction is preferred, h02 is the documented alternative. No spill, collision, grasp-loss, or unseen-error recovery was validated.

**Recognize failure:** No validation failures were observed, but the relevant terminal failure signature remains at least 10 particles transferred while the source is not upright, possibly still over the bowl. Also treat fewer than 10 settled particles, spill, loss of rigid holding, collision, or bad IK diagnostics as failure; closed fingers alone do not prove contact.

**Handoff:** Do not hand off on emptiness alone. Require at least 10 particles settled, the source itself approximately upright and securely held, and outbound motion toward the return region begun. Then invoke `return_place_release`, nominally near action 1680; [1460,1740) is jointly action-supervised for flexible takeover. This policy does not place or release the container.

validation.exit_rule: container above the bowl and upright with no particle in the bowl at the final state
validation.guidance:
**Primary/default candidate within the demonstrated entry distribution.** This dual-source/bowl-position, absolute-world-orientation policy satisfied the required final stage exit in 11/12 validation runs (91.7%). At the final state, all 12 runs were upright with zero particles in the bowl; 11/12 were also over the bowl. The sole failure remained upright and spill-free but did not reach the bowl footprint. All runs reported zero IK-unconverged steps.

Invoke only with finite, trustworthy container and bowl poses; nominally with an upright, table-supported source and open fingers, or from a nearby closed/low/lifted state when source/TCP co-motion is plausible. Handle geometry must be unchanged and the target must be reachable with collision clearance. The prior is designed to combine source-relative acquisition, bowl-relative staging, and absolute orientation, but robustness to displaced objects or other out-of-distribution states was not tested.

Avoid or stop for noisy/missing poses, changed geometry, large rotations, obstacles, unreachable configurations, grasp miss, slip/drop, or severe intermediate-state error. Recognize failure through closed fingers without source/TCP co-motion, failure to lift, abrupt or stalled transport, particle escape, loss of uprightness, staging outside the bowl footprint, IK nonconvergence, or joint-limit contact. Do not treat the internal destination/blend weight as proof of contact or phase.

Hand off to `controlled_pour_and_right` only when physical observations confirm closed fingers, source/TCP co-motion, table clearance, an upright container high over the bowl, and no particle in the bowl. If the container is upright but not over the bowl—as in the one validation failure—do not hand off; stop/escalate or reselect.

validation.exit_rule: standard task success at the final state (enough poured, container at the return region, upright)
validation.guidance: Observed reliability is poor: only 3/12 nominal in-distribution runs passed. All nine failures ended with the container outside the return region; four also ended non-upright and had 360–394 IK-unconverged steps, while the other five remained upright but still missed return. Failed runs showed 3–74 gripper-command changes versus one in each passing run. Therefore no reliably validated selection niche was identified, and this policy should not be the default when h01–h03 are available. Its intended source-frame niche—an accurately observed, securely grasped source with off-cluster source pose or source/TCP relation—is only a documented hypothesis; there is no out-of-distribution validation. If used experimentally, call `source_object="container", destination="target_pose"`, monitor every eight-action replan, and stop/switch on source/TCP separation, motion inconsistent with a closed-finger grasp, oscillating source-relative targets, no destination progress, repeated IK failure/limit contact, premature opening, post-release source motion, or retreat recontact; never chase a lost/free source. The documented switches are h02 when the source anchor is questionable and fresh-TCP correction is safer, h01 after righting when destination displacement dominates, and h03 near nominal support when release phase dominates. Even a transient success is insufficient: terminal handoff to evaluation requires observed upright stationary in-bounds support, open fingers, and TCP clearance.
